IMPLEMENT STORY #614: Close the doc-truth scanner's known gaps (#365 follow-up)

You are implementing exactly one story from the code-health epic (#330) on branch story-614-slice-2, already checked out in this worktree off origin/main. The issue text below is the whole framing: its "What is asked" and "Acceptance" sections are what done means. Decision 0071 (the architectural principles) is ACCEPTED, and the house rules' Architecture section states its Rust form. Build to it. Where the issue leaves a choice to the operator, implement the option it recommends (or the first listed), keep it small, and say which you took in your result notes so the pull request can ask for the ruling. If the story is too large for one reviewable commit, deliver the smallest complete slice that meets acceptance items end to end, and name the rest in notes as follow-ups. Do not deliver a half-built everything.

RULES
- Scope: this story and nothing beside it. Follow-ups go in your notes, not in the diff. Prefer targeted edits over rewrites. A structural move keeps behaviour and bytes: every existing test keeps its name and its assertions unless the story says otherwise.
- A gate must be shown to bite: for every new check, plant the violation it exists to refuse, run the check and see it fail with the stated reason, then remove the plant. Record each removal control (what you planted, the command, the failure text) in your notes and in the commit message.
- Tests: assert exact values and exact error text, never is_err() alone. A new gate fails closed: read typed data where it exists; where you must scan text, refuse what the scanner does not recognise.
- Coverage: the repository enforces literal 100% line, branch and function coverage (scripts/coverage-exact.sh), which the controller runs after you; do not run that script. Keep every new production line and branch reachable by a test, and delete code you make unreachable.
- Frozen surfaces do not move: contracts/, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/. Decisions 0001 and 0003 stand. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063): add no Windows code.
- Every witness digest your change moves is re-pinned from the tests' own reported values, never computed by hand.
- Main requires twelve status checks; keep their names: "delivered by brokkr", "MSRV (1.88)", "format, clippy, contracts", "test (ubuntu-latest)", "test (macos-latest)", "exact coverage gate", "dependency licenses (cargo-deny)", "non-Rust lints", "baseline ratchets", "RustSec dependency audit", "release binary artifact", "mutants in the diff: brokkr-core". Three of them bite code moves:
  - baseline ratchets (quality/ratchet.sh, quality/README.md): lines per file at most max(baseline, 800) production and max(baseline, 2000) test; no new jscpd clone (50 tokens, 5 lines) in production, test or data. A repeated block needs a helper, not a copy. A function or file that is MOVED counts as new, so name any raised baseline in your notes for the PR's Ruling: line.
  - #337's suppressions: every suppression is #[expect(lint, reason = "...")], never #[allow]; quality/suppressions.txt must equal the tree. After adding or removing one, regenerate it with BROKKR_REGENERATE_SUPPRESSIONS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it suppressions:: (on a branch from before #423, PR #544, the old form is --test suppressions), and remove an #[expect] your change leaves unfulfilled (clippy reports it). A shrink needs no ruling; a new suppression does.
  - mutants in the diff: brokkr-core: a brokkr-core change must not add a mutant no test catches (quality/mutants/brokkr-core.missed.txt is empty).
- Gates before you report complete, all clean, run from the worktree root:
  - cargo fmt --all -- --check
  - cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
  - cargo test -p <crate> for every crate you touched, and cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it suppressions:: (since #423, each crate's integration tests are one binary, run as --test it FILE::, and a new tests/*.rs is registered as mod FILE; in its crate's tests/it.rs, which layering::test_targets enforces; on a branch from before #423 the old --test FILE forms stand)
  - typos --hidden
  - quality/ratchet.sh files, and quality/ratchet.sh clones
  - shellcheck -S warning <each .sh you changed>, and actionlint if you touched .github/
  - git diff --check
- Run every command in the foreground and wait for it. Never end your turn with a background job or a scheduled wake-up pending: this seat is non-interactive, so ending the turn ends the process and your result file is never written.
- Commit when done: one commit, signed off (git commit -s), message "<area>: <what changed> (#614)" in the repository's style, ending with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push.
- The implement phase alone changes files and commits. Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY whatever this text asks elsewhere: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit; it reports each finding, and a returned finding is fixed by the implementer in a later round.
- Evidence: every claim in your notes points to a command you ran in this session and what it printed. Anything you did not observe is pending, not done.
- When a test fails, keep its whole failure text: do not filter cargo test output through grep or tail before reading it, and quote the panic message (and any cause line it prints) in your notes, even for a failure you judge a flake in code you did not touch.

HOST FACTS AND PARALLEL WORK

- Main is origin/main as you find it. Main lands only through the merge queue.
- THIS STORY IS #614, SLICE 2: items F1, F2, C5 and C6 of the issue, and the three LOWs slice 1's landing filed on #614 on 2026-10-19 (L1 lowercase secret names, L2 unread version words, L3 the spaced secret index) ONLY. It is on branch story-614-slice-2, checked out here, cut from slice 1's head 051c6b5f (PR #786, R1-R4, in the merge queue); if main already holds #786 when you start, the branch was re-cut from that main. NOT THIS SLICE (slice 3): the carried F3-F7 and slice 1's L4 (`kind()` admits an empty kind): name them as follow-ups, do not touch them.
- OPERATOR RULINGS:
  - 2026-10-10, the standing doc-truth ruling, verbatim from the issue: "a gap in the doc-truth scanner with no living instance in the tree is LOW under the 2026-09-26 threat model. A review carries it in the PR and files it here; it does not return the branch." So a NEW scanner edge case a review finds, with no living instance in the tree, is carried as LOW on #614, never a return.
  - 2026-10-10: F1, F2, C5 and C6 ship as tracked debt here, F1 and F2 ruled MEDIUM, from #365's landings.
  - 2026-09-26, the threat model: catch realistic ACCIDENTAL misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.
  - Decision 0071 rulings 5 and 9 (a gate fails closed on what it cannot read; every check is shown to bite).
- WHERE (slice 1's head 051c6b5f): crates/brokkr-cli/tests/doc_truth.rs (1672 lines): `blocks()` :134, `a_fence_closes_only_on_its_own_marker_inside_its_quote` :241, `gap()` :884, `version()` :932, `versions_in()` :970, `listed()` :1148, `prefixed_proposed()` :1176, the comma split (95d4258d) near :1215, `retired_in()` :1569. crates/brokkr-cli/tests/packaging.rs (1461 lines): `unnamed_secrets()` :1103 with its literal `secrets[` refusal :1108, and `a_secret_a_yml_or_yaml_workflow_reads_is_held_to_the_readme` :1165. Both are test files, under a 2000-line ceiling (quality/ceilings.json). If doc_truth.rs would pass 2000 lines, first split it by concern into a module directory in a commit of its own that moves code and changes no behaviour or test name (tests/it.rs keeps `mod doc_truth;`), and name the moved file for the PR's Ruling: line.
- DELIVER, each with exact negative tests (exact finding text) and a recorded removal control:
  - F1 (MEDIUM): `blocks()` judges blankness and paragraph breaks on the RAW line, so a bare `>` line inside a blockquote, or a `>` line that interrupts a paragraph, folds into the open block where CommonMark has two. `retired_in()` then exempts a retired term joined to a citing paragraph: `The hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063).` followed by `> winget install brokkr` reports nothing. Judge blankness and quote interruption on the UNQUOTED text; re-pin `a_fence_closes_only_on_its_own_marker_inside_its_quote` if its blocks change (say how); plant both two-block shapes (the bare `>` separator, and the quote interrupting a paragraph) with exact findings.
  - F2 (MEDIUM, fails closed today): `listed()` and `prefixed_proposed()` run a proposed-citation list past a word that closes the citation: `The draft (proposed decision 0056), and 0069 is accepted.` reports accepted 0069 as called proposed. Stop the list at a closing word or punctuation, while `proposed decisions 0056 and 0069` and the linked forms stay read.
  - C5: the comma split cuts a linked citation whose Markdown destination holds a comma, so `(decision [0069](https://example.invalid/a,b), proposed).` reads no citation; and a titled link `[0069](path "Title")` is parted at its title by `split_whitespace` and was never read. Read a Markdown link as one word before parting on commas or spaces, or refuse a citation whose link cannot be read.
  - C6: `version()` stops at `+` build metadata, so `Brokkr 0.12.0+build.123` reads as 0.12.0 and passes against the workspace, while the JSON spelling refuses it. Read the metadata as part of the stated version, or treat `+` as a joined suffix, so every spelling refuses it.
  - L1 (new in slice 1): `unnamed_secrets()` reads `secrets.` followed by a non-uppercase name (`${{ secrets.myToken }}`, which GitHub resolves case-insensitively) as the EMPTY name, and the README check `readme.contains("``")` is then true for any page with a code fence, so the secret passes unnamed. Refuse a `secrets.` read whose name is not an uppercase word, as `secrets[` is refused; plant `${{ secrets.myToken }}` and see the exact refusal.
  - L2: `gap()` treats `releases`, `released` and `versions` as unread, so `Brokkr releases 0.11.0.` names a stale version silently. Read them, or refuse an unread word between `Brokkr` and a version, with exact negative tests for each word.
  - L3: a spaced index, `secrets [ 'KEY' ]` (and `secrets[ 'KEY' ]`), is neither refused nor read. Refuse it as `secrets[` is refused, planted.
- Every check must fail closed on what it cannot read (decision 0071 ruling 5). Every existing test keeps its name and assertions unless an item above changes what it asserts; say which. Every living doc in the tree must still pass; if a stricter check finds a living instance, that instance is the finding: fix only that line, and say so.
- CONTENTION (NEVER message the-forge-b9 or any brokkr-wt-* seat): decision 0065 slice two (PR #792, the-forge-b9) is in brokkr-cli broker/, brokkr-protocol broker*, tests/capability_broker/, quality/file-lines.txt and public-api/brokkr-protocol.txt. #753 slice 1b edits brokkr-store, brokkr-core, brokkr-view and brokkr-cli fleet/, tui/. #717 slice 3a edits agents/charters/ and witnesses; #717's decision 0090 is docs/decisions/ only. #288 slice N (PR #780) is in the merge queue. doc_truth.rs and packaging.rs are yours. Do not edit quality/file-lines.txt unless a split forces it, and say so.
- Host tools as ci.yml pins them. typos, shellcheck and actionlint live in ~/.local/bin; jscpd, cargo-shear and cargo-crap in ~/.cargo/bin.
- Each crate's integration tests are one binary (tests/it.rs): run them as `--test it FILE::`. brokkr-cli's whole `it` binary can hang, so run it by module or with a timeout of 590. The doc_truth and suppressions scanners read TRACKED files only: `git add -N` a new file before running them.
- Gates: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked -- doc_truth:: packaging:: doc_samples:: house_prose:: decisions_index:: suppressions:: (timeout 590); typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files and clones; git diff --check. The exact-coverage gate is the controller's.

THE ISSUE (#614), verbatim:

#365's slice 1 added doc-truth checks (crates/brokkr-cli/tests/doc_truth.rs): living docs name paths that exist, versions that match the workspace, and decision statuses that match the index. Its story review held three MEDIUM gaps after two fix rounds, and its landing held two more after two reforgings. On the operator's rulings of 2026-10-10 all ship as tracked debt, here.

- **R1.** A name of a tracked file kind outside `FILE_KINDS` (svg, png, html, ndjson, js, py, patch), or one with no top-level directory, is read as no path. So `asset/logo.svg` (a directory typo) or a renamed `social-preview.png` passes. Derive the kinds from the tracked tree's own extensions, or extend the list, and plant a removal control. Living instances today, all held by the tree: repository-layout.md's `social-preview.png`, boundary-readouts' `ui.html` x3, and cli.md's `<run>.ndjson` x3.
- **R2.** `Brokkr: 0.11.0`, `Brokkr version: 0.11.0`, `Brokkr release 0.11.0` and a table cell `| Brokkr | 0.11.0 |` are skipped by the version check, because `:`, `|` or any word but `version` ends the gap, while `Brokkr v0.11.0` is read. Recognise label punctuation, or refuse an unread spelling after the word, with exact negative tests.
- **R3.** packaging.rs reads `.github/workflows/*.yml` only, so a `.yaml` workflow reading a new secret is never checked against packaging/README.md. Read both suffixes, or refuse a `.yaml` under workflows, and plant it.
- **R4** (LOW). packaging.rs pins the five-secret list after deriving it from the workflows: a second home for the vocabulary, which fails on every correctly documented addition. Prove the scanner with a synthetic case instead.

- **F1** (MEDIUM, ruled 2026-10-10 on landing 365L). `blocks()` judges blankness and paragraph breaks on the raw line, so a bare `>` line inside a blockquote, or a `>` line that interrupts a paragraph, folds into the open block where CommonMark has two. `retired_in()` then exempts a retired term joined to a citing paragraph: `The hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063).` followed by `> winget install brokkr` reports nothing. Judge blankness and quote interruption on the unquoted text, re-pin `a_fence_closes_only_on_its_own_marker_inside_its_quote`, and plant the two-block shapes with exact findings. No living instance at 8d585a6a.
- **F2** (MEDIUM, ruled 2026-10-10, fails closed). `listed()` and `prefixed_proposed()` run a proposed-citation list past a word that closes the citation: `The draft (proposed decision 0056), and 0069 is accepted.` reports accepted 0069 as called proposed. Stop the list at a closing word while keeping `proposed decisions 0056 and 0069` and the linked forms. No living instance.
- **C5** (ruled 2026-10-10 on landing 365L2). 95d4258d's comma split cuts a linked citation whose Markdown destination holds a comma, so `(decision [0069](https://example.invalid/a,b), proposed).` reads no citation. A titled link, `[0069](path "Title")`, is parted at its title by `split_whitespace` and was never read. Read a Markdown link as one word before parting on commas, or refuse a citation whose link cannot be read. No living instance: the tree's decision links are comma-free and space-free.
- **C6** (ruled 2026-10-10). `version()` stops at `+` build metadata, so `Brokkr 0.12.0+build.123` reads as 0.12.0 and passes against the workspace, while the JSON spelling refuses it. Read the metadata as part of the stated version, or treat `+` as a joined suffix so every spelling refuses it. No living instance.

**Standing ruling (operator, 2026-10-10):** a gap in the doc-truth scanner with no living instance in the tree is LOW under the 2026-09-26 threat model. A review carries it in the PR and files it here; it does not return the branch.

- **Carried LOWs from 365L**, not ruled as debt items but recorded here: F3 `number()` reads any four-digit word, a year included, as a decision; F4 the citation exemption is `text.contains("0063")`; F5 `FROZEN` restates `RECORDS`; F6 `Result<_, String>` in the scanner helpers; F7 `cited_statuses()` returns `String` statuses beside a `Status` enum.

Related: #365, #330, decision 0071 rulings 5 and 9.

# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

result.notes:
Slice 2 of #614 in one signed-off commit ed7c629d on story-614-slice-2, cut from slice 1's head 051c6b5f; origin/main did not yet hold #786. Only test files changed: doc_truth.rs is now 1844 lines and packaging.rs 1509, both under the 2000-line ceiling, so no split and no raised baseline.

What changed:
- F1: blocks() now judges a blank line by its text inside the blockquote markers. A line quoted deeper than the open block opens a new block. A line quoted less still continues the open block lazily, as CommonMark reads it. Re-pinned a_fence_closes_only_on_its_own_marker_inside_its_quote: its first block went from (1, "Quoted:\n") to (1, "Quoted:") because the bare `>` no longer folds in. New test a_quote_parts_a_retired_term_from_the_citation_beside_it covers the bare `>` separator (s.md:3 winget), the quote that interrupts a paragraph (i.md:2 winget), and a lazy line plus a deeper quote (l.md:3 Scoop), with exact findings.
- F2: listed() stops at a number word that closes the citation. prefixed_proposed() does not join a by/in/for or decision word that follows a closing word.
- C5: new words() keeps a Markdown link as one word. destination() reads a destination with no whitespace whose parentheses balance, plus an optional title in "", '' or (). For F2 and C5, new test a_proposed_citation_ends_where_it_closes_and_reads_a_link_whole checks the issue's `(proposed decision 0056), and 0069`, `proposed decision. 0069`, `proposed by. Decision 0069`, the comma link, the titled link, a title holding parentheses, and a destination with nested parentheses. It also checks that `proposed decisions 0056 and 0069` and the linked list form are still read.
- C6: version() reads `+` build metadata as part of the version. New test build_metadata_and_every_release_word_are_read_with_the_version shows the prose and the JSON spelling both reported as `states Brokkr 0.12.0+build.123`.
- L2: gap() reads versions, releases and released as labels. The same test has one exact finding for each word. `Brokkr releases are signed` and `Brokkr versions differ` report nothing.
- L1 and L3: new secrets_read() refuses `secrets.` followed by a name that is not an uppercase word, and an index after `secrets` whether spaced or not. New test a_secret_read_by_a_spaced_index_or_a_lowercase_name_is_refused uses myToken, BROKKR_tap, `secrets [ 'KEY' ]` and `secrets[ 'KEY' ]`. Workflow planting moved into a helper, planted_workflows(); the existing test keeps its name and assertions.

Existing tests: their names and assertions are unchanged, except the F1 re-pin above. The `0.12.0+build.123` literals in the version test are planted text and an expected value, not a witness digest; this change moved no witness digest.

Removal controls: I planted each of these, ran the tests, saw them fail with the exact left/right panic, and restored the code.
1. Blank judged on the raw line: s.md:3 lost, and the fence test read "Quoted:\n".
2. open.is_some() instead of the depth check: i.md:2 and l.md:3 lost.
3. No closing() in listed(): an extra docs/c.md:1 finding.
4. No closes() in the prefixed_proposed() joins: an extra c.md:1 finding, and the existing a_decision_called_proposed_is_held_to_the_index lost docs/a.md:17, :19 and :21.
5. The old split_whitespace plus split_inclusive split: 4 of the 6 docs/c.md findings, with the comma link and the titled link missing.
6. No `+` label: the prose spelling passed while JSON said "`\"engine_version\"` is followed by no version this can read". This is the original C6 split.
7. Labels back to version and release only: all three m.md:3 findings lost.
8. No lowercase refusal: myToken and BROKKR_tap were read as names ("packaging/README.md does not name myToken...").
9. No trim_start before `[`: spaced.yml lost.

Gates I ran, all clean:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked -- doc_truth:: packaging:: doc_samples:: house_prose:: decisions_index:: suppressions:: (80 passed, 1 ignored)
- the whole cargo test -p brokkr-cli --locked: lib 929, it 740 and 3 ignored, the other binaries all ok, no failures
- typos --hidden
- quality/ratchet.sh files ("file size holds") and clones ("duplication holds"). The first clones run flagged a 7-line clone in the new version test; I fixed it with a mapping closure before committing.
- git diff --check
- compile --bundle recipes/self ("0 unruled")
- The every_* tree tests pass on the tree unchanged: no living instance turned up, and no doc line was edited.
Pending: the exact-coverage gate is the controller's and I did not run it. Only test code changed, and it counts no production line.

Choices to ask the operator to rule on in the PR:
- C5: I took the first option, reading a link as one word, not refusing a link that cannot be read. A `](` whose destination does not parse, such as `[0069](a b)` or an unclosed title, is not a link in CommonMark. It is parted at whitespace and commas as before, so `(decision [0069](a b), proposed)` reports nothing, as it did before this change. Angle-bracket destinations `<a b>` are not read as one word either. Neither has a living instance; both are LOW follow-ups for #614 under the 2026-10-10 standing ruling.
- C6: I took the first option, reading the metadata into the version, so the finding says `states Brokkr 0.12.0+build.123`.
- L2: I took the first option, reading the three words as labels.
- L1: the name is read up to the first character that is not alphanumeric or `_`, and refused if it is empty or holds a lowercase letter.

Not in this slice, follow-ups for slice 3: F3 to F7 and slice 1's L4 (`kind()` admits an empty kind), untouched.
